what_its_for: Ergotamine is used to treat migraine headaches and cluster headaches. It works by narrowing the blood vessels in your brain, which helps stop the pain and other symptoms of a migraine, such as nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound. It works best when taken at the very first sign of a headache.
how_to_take: Take ergotamine exactly as your doctor tells you. It comes as a tablet that dissolves under your tongue (sublingual) or a suppository inserted into the rectum. Do NOT swallow the sublingual tablet — place it under your tongue and let it dissolve completely. Do not eat, drink, or smoke while the tablet is dissolving. If using the suppository form, follow the instructions given to you by your pharmacist or doctor. Always take this medicine at the first sign of a migraine headache. Do not take it daily or as a regular pain reliever.
dosing: The usual adult dose for sublingual tablets is 2 mg (one tablet) placed under the tongue at the first sign of a migraine. You may take an additional 2 mg tablet every 30 minutes if needed, but do NOT take more than 3 tablets (6 mg) for a single attack. Do NOT take more than 5 mg (two and a half tablets) in one week. Your doctor may adjust your dose. Never take more than prescribed — overuse can make headaches worse and cause serious side effects.
missed_dose: Ergotamine is not taken on a regular daily schedule — you only take it when you feel a migraine coming on. If you forgot to take it at the very start of your headache, take it as soon as you remember. However, if your headache is already in full swing, the medicine may not work as well. Do not double up your dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store ergotamine tablets and suppositories at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine past its expiration date.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking while taking ergotamine, as it can increase the risk of serious blood vessel problems. Do not drink grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of ergotamine in your blood to dangerous levels. Avoid other migraine medicines (like triptans such as sumatriptan) within 24 hours of taking ergotamine. Do not take ergotamine with strong antibiotics like erythromycin or clarithromycin, antifungal medicines like ketoconazole, or HIV medicines, as these can cause dangerous interactions. Avoid taking more than the prescribed dose — overuse can lead to a condition called medication overuse headache (rebound headache). Limit alcohol use as it may worsen headaches.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, tightness, or pressure; numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arms or legs; sudden severe headache worse than usual; vision changes; fast or irregular heartbeat; swelling; severe stomach pain; cold, pale, or blue fingers or toes; signs of poor circulation (pain in your legs when walking). Also call your doctor if your headaches are getting more frequent or are not improving, or if you feel you need to take this medicine more than twice a week.
when_it_works: Ergotamine works best when taken at the very first warning sign of a migraine, such as an aura (visual changes, flashing lights) or the first hint of head pain. It usually starts to relieve pain within 30 minutes to 2 hours. It does NOT prevent migraines from occurring — it only treats them once they start.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use ergotamine if you are pregnant. It can cause serious harm to your baby, including premature labor or birth defects. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: Do not use ergotamine while breastfeeding, as it passes into breast milk and can harm your baby. Children: Safety in children has not been well established. Talk to your doctor before giving this medicine to anyone under 18. Older Adults: Use with caution in older adults, as they may be more sensitive to blood vessel side effects. Kidney or Liver Problems: Do NOT use ergotamine if you have significant liver or kidney disease. Heart or Blood Vessel Problems: This medicine is NOT safe for people with coronary artery disease, high blood pressure, or peripheral vascular disease. Always tell your doctor your full medical history before starting this medicine.
